candidate_sentence_map.S1: AAC Clyde Space reported a decline in financial performance for the year 2025, driven by operational delays and a strategic shift in revenue recognition timing.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Net sales decreased by 16 percent to SEK 295.3 million, down from SEK 352.9 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: This reduction was primarily caused by delays in the Products & Missions segment, where technical discussions and procurement postponements shifted approximately SEK 32 million in revenue to 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Specifically, the EPS-Sterna programme initiation was delayed due to political and procurement developments, and a separate customer project milestone was postponed.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Despite the lower top line, the Data & Services segment demonstrated strong growth, with net sales increasing by 78 percent to SEK 80.1 million from SEK 44.9 million in the prior year.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: This growth reflects the company’s expanding capability to design, build, and operate its own satellite systems, generating recurring revenue streams.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: The Group’s profitability metrics reflected the impact of these delays and increased investment activities.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: EBITDA fell significantly to SEK 17.5 million from SEK 46.7 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: The operating result after depreciation and impairment was a loss of SEK 40.0 million, compared to a loss of SEK 4.0 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: The loss after tax amounted to SEK 46.6 million, resulting in earnings per share of negative SEK 7.63, compared to negative SEK 1.00 in the previous year.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Operating cash flow also deteriorated, moving from a positive SEK 56.8 million in 2024 to a negative SEK 72.6 million in 2025, largely due to the timing of revenue recognition and working capital changes associated with project delays.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Key business developments during the period included the signing of a Phase 1 contract with the European Space Agency for the INFLECION programme, aimed at developing a satellite constellation for maritime intelligence.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: The company also received an order for long-lead components for the EPS-Sterna weather constellation and began assembly of its first VIREON™ Earth Observation satellites.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: The Sedna-1 and Sedna-2 satellites became fully operational, strengthening the maritime data network.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: To support these investments and ensure liquidity, the company completed two directed share issues, raising approximately SEK 114.8 million before transaction costs.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Notably, Bonnier Capital became a major shareholder through a strategic investment.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: The equity ratio improved to 80 percent from 71 percent, indicating a strengthened balance sheet despite the operational losses.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Order backlog stood at SEK 352 million at year-end, though the CEO noted that a major contract awarded in early 2026 would significantly increase this figure.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: The company maintained a strong focus on capital discipline while expanding its constellation capacity to meet growing demand for space-based data services.
